title: Numbers print with six significant digits, which changes values written with more and prints `10e-23`
impact: No reactions, no project named; one of the #1391-#1406 batch filed by the same reporter on 2026-10-27, likely agent-found. The underlying precision issue is real and tracked in #949 (6 reactions, 8 comments; see also closed #917). The reporter's values (8 significant digits, 9.9999999e-23px) are not realistic; realistic impact comes from repeating fractions like calc(4/3) or calc(100%/3), which #949 covers.
code: src/values/number.rs: CSSNumber::to_css (via cssparser ToCss for f32 -> dtoa_short, 6 significant digits)
summary: Every number is printed with cssparser's 6-significant-digit serialization, so 1234.5678px -> 1234.57px and 99999.99px -> 100000px. Same root cause as #949. The only new detail is cosmetic: a value that rounds up across a power of ten in exponent form prints `10e-23px` instead of `1e-22px` (valid CSS, Chromium reads it back as 1e-22px, just 1 byte longer); no realistic stylesheet has such values.
evidence: scripts/repro.mjs on local (master), 1.33.0, 1.32.0, 1.31.1: identical output, all precision cases WRONG per the #949 direction, control correct. probe.mjs: Chromium accepts `10e-23px` and serializes it as `1e-22px`. Aside, not in the issue: serialize_dimension uses `value as i32` for int_value, so `left:1e21px` prints `2147483647px` (saturating cast); browsers clamp such lengths anyway, so no visible effect, fringe.

fix.approach: Per the maintainer's #949 position: don't print more digits; keep calc() as written or reduce the fraction for repeating decimals (calc(100% / 3)). The 10e-23 exponent normalization would belong in dtoa_short/cssparser (upstream) and isn't worth doing on its own.

subcases.case: 6-digit rounding of author-written values / repeating decimals

subcases.status: cosmetic, valid CSS, unrealistic input; not worth tracking separately

draftReply:
Thanks for the detailed report! This is the same root cause as #949, so I'll close this in favor of that issue to keep the discussion in one place.

The 6-digit serialization matches how CSSOM serializes numbers, but browsers compute at higher precision, so rounding can shift layout slightly. The direction discussed in #949 is not to print more digits, but to keep the expression when rounding would lose information, e.g. keep `calc(100% / 3)` instead of printing `33.3333%`. That is shorter and exact.

The `10e-23px` output is valid CSS (browsers read it as `1e-22px`), only a byte longer, and only happens for values far below anything a stylesheet would use.
